subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.memoText:

• Also accept: 0 / zero / 0° of longitude / UTC

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the 0º line of latitude located close to Ghana.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the line of latitude in QUESTION 2.1.1(b) is considered important for travel planning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Tourists must pack clothing suitable for the season during the time in which they travel, e.g. heat, humidity and rain.
• Tourists must protect themselves against all climate conditions when travelling to areas close to the equator.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, correct reason linked to climate/weather near the equator.]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO official travel documents the South Africans needed when they travelled to Ghana. (Ghana is a high-risk yellow fever area and South African tourists require an entry document in their passports to enter Ghana.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Valid passport
• Valid visa
• Health certificate (yellow fever certificate)
[Award 2 marks per correctly named official travel document.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Visitors from New York used their cellphones to do a live broadcast of the festival. This was broadcast from Accra at 21:00 to family and friends in New York on 9 August 2023.

Calculate the time and date the family and friends in New York watched the live broadcast from Accra.

Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Time difference identification — New York (USA) is at -5; Accra (Ghana) at 0° → Time Difference = 5 hours
Mark 2: Subtraction operation: Time in Accra 21:00 (− 5) hours
Mark 3: Time in New York = 16:00
Mark 4: Date in New York = 9 August 2023

Final answer: 16:00 on 9 August 2023
[Award full 4 marks for the correct final answer 16:00 on 9 August 2023 with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:
A Malawian music group was invited to the 2023 Homowo Festival in Ghana. They departed from Lilongwe, Malawi at 20:00 on 12 August 2023. The flying time was 12 hours (including a stopover).

Calculate the local time and date that this flight arrived in Accra, Ghana. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Time zone identification — Ghana 0°; Malawi +2 → Time Difference = 2 hours (DST does NOT apply)
Mark 2: Subtraction operation from Malawi to Ghana — Departure time 20:00 (− 2 hours)
Mark 3: Local time in Accra at departure = 18:00
Mark 4: Add flying time: 18:00 (+ 12 hours)
Mark 5: Arrival time = 06:00
Mark 6: Arrival date = 13 August 2023

Final answer: 06:00 on 13 August 2023
[Award full 6 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the exchange rate table:
| Country | Currency Code | BBR | BSR |
| Portugal | EUR | 18,10 | 18,75 |

Mr Da Sousa, a South African outbound tourist, is going to Portugal. Before his departure from South Africa, he exchanges ZAR35 500,00 at a forex kiosk at the OR Tambo International Airport.

Calculate how much he will receive in euro when he exchanges his foreign currency. (Round off to TWO decimal places.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify correct rate to use — Bank Selling Rate (BSR) = 18,75 (since Mr Da Sousa is BUYING foreign currency)
Mark 2: Division operation: ZAR35 500 ÷ 18,75
Mark 3 & 4: Final answer: €1 893,33

Final answer: €1 893,33
NOTE: Do not penalise the learner if the currency symbol or code is not indicated, as the currency is mentioned in the question.
[Award full 4 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:
On his return to South Africa, Mr Da Sousa exchanges the remaining 248 euro for rand at the OR Tambo International Airport.

Calculate the amount that he will receive in rand. (Round off to TWO decimal places.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify correct rate to use — Bank Buying Rate (BBR) = 18,10 (since Mr Da Sousa is SELLING euro back to the bank)
Mark 2: Multiplication operation: €248 × 18,10
Mark 3 & 4: Final answer: R4 488,80

Final answer: R4 488,80
NOTE: Do not penalise the learner if the currency symbol or code is not indicated, as the currency is mentioned in the question.
[Award full 4 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

• Glass bottles are re-usable.
• Use of plastic bottles is reduced.
• Less plastic is sent to the landfills.
• Less pollution.
• Long-term financial benefits.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained positive impact on waste management.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways how the discarding of single-use plastics at the hotel can create entrepreneurial opportunities for local communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Local communities can be involved in the collection and recycling process.
• They can sell the collected plastics.
• They can repurpose the plastics, e.g. handicrafts.
[Award 2 marks per fully discussed entrepreneurial opportunity.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'PLASTIC BOTTLES – FRIEND OR ENEMY?' infographic (151 billion litres of oil used yearly; 3 litres of water to make 1 plastic bottle; 100 million plastic bottles used worldwide every day; only 1 in 5 recycled; 80% end up in landfill or the ocean; 500 years for plastic to degrade).

Identify ONE fossil fuel used in the production of plastic bottles.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Oil
• Crude oil
• Petroleum

subQuestions.questionText:
Environmental organisations list plastic as the number one threat to our marine environment.

Give TWO examples of how plastics can threaten our marine environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• The animals mistake the plastic for food and it cannot be digested.
• Animals get caught/tangled in plastic and this limits their movement.
• The plastic gets stuck in their mouths and prevents marine life from feeding.
• The beaches can be polluted by plastic.
• Plastic takes a long time to degrade.
• It is a threat to their ecosystem.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained example of marine threat.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'PARIS 2024 – GAMES WIDE OPEN' extract (Olympic Games: 26 July to 11 August 2024; Paralympic Games: 28 August to 8 September 2024) and the 'MASCOTS OF THE 2024 OLYMPIC GAMES' picture showing two mascots labelled A and B.

Refer to the dates of the 2024 Olympic Games. Give ONE reason why it is called the Summer Olympics.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
July, August and September are summer months in the Northern Hemisphere.
[Award 2 marks for a clear reason linking the dates to summer in the Northern Hemisphere where Paris is located.]

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between the Olympic Games and the Paralympic Games in terms of participants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• The Olympic Games are aimed at abled-bodied athletes and the Paralympic Games caters for participants who are differently abled.
• Olympic Games are for participants without physical challenges and the Paralympic Games are for participants with physical challenges.
[Award 2 marks for a clear differentiation covering BOTH games' participants.]

subQuestions.label: 9.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The mascots for the Olympic Games and the Paralympic Games are marked A and B.

Identify the mascot that represents the Paralympic Games.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (2 marks): B

subQuestions.label: 9.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for your answer to QUESTION 9.1.3(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Mascot B has prosthesis on both legs, indicating it is physically challenged.
• Mascot B has a prosthesis on one leg, indicating it is physically challenged.
[Award 2 marks for correctly identifying the prosthetic feature on Mascot B.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE economic benefit for a country hosting a global event.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• It will bring more foreign income to the country.
• It will create awareness of the hosting nation.
• Publicity for the country helps to attract tourists.
• Investment in the country boosts economic growth.
• Tourism creates job opportunities for locals.
• Increased GDP strengthens the national economy.
• Tourism sets the multiplier effect into motion, benefiting various sectors.
• Infrastructure development improves facilities for both locals and tourists.
[Award 2 marks for a fully discussed economic benefit.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'INTERNATIONAL TOURIST ARRIVALS TO SOUTH AFRICA — JULY TO SEPTEMBER 2022' infographic (Africa Land 73%, Africa Air 3%, Europe 13%, Americas 6%, Asia 2%, Australasia 1%, Middle East 1%; 11% Geographic Spread).

Explain the meaning of international tourist arrivals to South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
It refers to tourists who are entering South Africa from other countries.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, accurate explanation.]

subQuestions.label: 9.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why a country such as Ghana is considered an African air market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
Majority of the visitors from Ghana reach South Africa by air transport.
[Award 2 marks for an explanation linking Ghana to air travel.]

subQuestions.label: 9.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why a country such as Botswana is considered an African land market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
Majority of the visitors from Botswana reach South Africa by land transport e.g. road or rail transport.
[Award 2 marks for an explanation linking Botswana to land transport (a shared border with South Africa).]

subQuestions.questionText: Excluding the African markets, identify the continent with the highest percentage of arrivals.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (2 marks): Europe (13%)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE way in which the visitor numbers from Australasia and the Middle East (at 1%) can be increased.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• More focused marketing campaigns
• More exposure of what South Africa has to offer for tourists.
• Packages that will suit the preferences/needs of the people in Australasia and the Middle East.
• More flights to South Africa.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, viable suggestion.]

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the method identified in QUESTION 10.1 (customer feedback).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Customer feedback is the information provided by customers about their experiences of a product or service.
• It is an evaluation of a customer's level of satisfaction with a product or service.
• It is an opinion about a product or service.
[Award 2 marks for a clear explanation of customer feedback.]

subQuestions.questionText:
There are several methods used to rate customer services. Refer to the SURVEY and CELLPHONE icons.

Compare the effectiveness of the TWO methods of responses indicated below (Survey vs Cellphone).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (2 marks each — total 4 marks):

Survey (any ONE — 2 marks):
• It is an easy way to get a response.
• Customers may prefer filling in a survey instead of sharing phone details or other contact details.
• Customers feel as though their comments matter.
• Do not have to use data.

Cellphone (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Immediate feedback about the company/product/service.
• It is an instant response.
• Makes the customers feel like they were heard.

[Award 2 marks per correctly explained effectiveness — one mark allocation per method.]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE positive impact of customer responses on a business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Customer responses will inform the business where their problems are.
• It will inform the business on ways to correct their problems.
• It will give insight into the company's weak areas or poor service delivery.
• It will allow the company to adjust its products/services to improve service delivery.
[Award 2 marks for a clearly explained positive impact.]
